title: Fix config reload state imports (#7028)
author: harsh21234i

unresolved.first_comment: P1: When an older RegistrationContext is re-entered after another same-project context has loaded, ctx._config is None is false, so _get_config retains the globally cached dependency modules from the newer context.
Too long comments, explaining what is already can be seen in code. happens in many places. we might want to clean up these.

ctx._config is None is the wrong signal. RegistrationContext.fork() copies base_states but resets _config to None, so a forked context re-triggers the same StateValueError. This is the path AppHarness takes. Please key the decision on whether the current context already holds the states those modules registered.
The _config_module_deps_root != project_root branch is not exercised; with the comparison removed, all 118 tests in test_config.py still pass. Either drop it or add a test that actually reaches it.
Both calls use reload_dependencies=True, so this test passes on main too and does not cover the new root check.

outstanding_asks.ask: Reproduced the cubic P1 with the #7028 repro, found the fix also fails through RegistrationContext.fork() (the AppHarness path), and found the new project-root eviction branch is untested and possibly dead. Rework the fix to key on whether the current context already holds the registered states, not on ctx._config is None.
